missing_spec_content.spec_text: Students should be able to draw and interpret circuit diagrams.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson never shows or explains a circuit diagram. Symbols are only described in words in tables[0] (for example "Rectangle", "Triangle + vertical bar"), and every keyPoints diagram field is null. There is no teaching on drawing or interpreting a complete circuit diagram.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: explain the design and use of a circuit to measure the resistance of a component by measuring the current through, and potential difference across, the component
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson gives R = V ÷ I but does not describe the measuring circuit. It never says the ammeter goes in series with the component, the voltmeter goes in parallel across it, or that R is calculated from these readings.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: draw an appropriate circuit diagram using correct circuit symbols.
missing_spec_content.why: No ammeter, voltmeter, cell, battery or switch symbols are taught, and there is no guidance on drawing a circuit diagram.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: Required practical activity 4: use circuit diagrams to construct appropriate circuits to investigate the I–V characteristics of a variety of circuit elements, including a filament lamp, a diode and a resistor at constant temperature.
missing_spec_content.why: The required practical is not taught. There is no method, no circuit, no use of a variable resistor to vary the current, no reversing of connections to get negative potential differences, and no step of plotting I against V.

above_gcse.text: Then there is a sudden steep rise once the forward threshold potential difference is passed.
above_gcse.why: The specification only requires that a diode conducts in one direction and has very high resistance in the reverse direction. A named 'forward threshold potential difference', given as a key term with its own definition, goes beyond the specification text.

factual_errors.correction: The standard thermistor symbol is a rectangle with a diagonal line through it that ends in a short horizontal tail (a 'hockey-stick' shape). A plain diagonal line is incomplete and is easily confused with the variable resistor symbol.

wrong_terms.spec_term: light intensity ("The resistance of an LDR decreases as light intensity increases.")

not_checked: All keyPoints diagram fields are null and circuit symbols are described only in words in tables[0], so the accuracy of any drawn symbols or I-V graph sketches could not be checked.

The filament lamp I-V curve is described only in words in tables[1] ("Curve — gets less steep at higher current"). Without a graph, it could not be checked whether the lesson shows the curve passing through the origin and being symmetrical for negative potential differences.
